content.user_title: Review Code Across Quality, Security, Performance
content.value_statement: Code reviews often miss security, accessibility, and performance issues when scope is broad. This skill routes review work to focused checklists and produces prioritized findings.
actual_capabilities: Routes review requests to quality, security, performance, accessibility, or change-review guidance.
Provides structured checklists for OWASP-style, TypeScript, React, and accessibility concerns.
Suggests command-line checks such as git diff, TypeScript, ESLint, and Prettier.
Supports parallel subagent review when several files need multiple review perspectives.
Formats findings with severity, file references, recommendations, and score-style summaries.
limitations: Guidance depends on available project files and tool permissions.
Command examples may require project-specific package scripts or installed dependencies.
It cannot guarantee complete vulnerability discovery without human validation.
Some guidance is written in Japanese and may require translation for other teams.

use_cases.title: Pre-merge pull request review
use_cases.description: Review changed files for security, quality, performance, accessibility, and consistency before merging.

use_cases.title: Release readiness check
use_cases.description: Focus review attention on risky areas such as authentication, APIs, database access, and user interface changes.

use_cases.title: Self-review before handoff
use_cases.description: Run a structured checklist to identify missing tests, unsafe patterns, and cleanup tasks before sharing work.

prompt_templates.title: Review my changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of recent local edits.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current changes for quality, security, performance, accessibility, and missing tests. Prioritize findings that should block a merge.

prompt_templates.title: Check a pull request
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused review for a pull request or branch diff.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this branch diff against the target branch. Group findings by severity, cite files and lines, and include concrete fixes.

prompt_templates.title: Audit risky areas
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of sensitive application paths.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the authentication, API, database, and user input changes. Focus on injection, authorization, secret exposure, and unsafe error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Run multi-perspective review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across several changed files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run separate quality, security, performance, and accessibility reviews for these changes. Merge the results into one prioritized review report.

output_examples.input: Review a five-file pull request that changes an API route and a React form.
output: High: Authorization is missing on the updated API route. Add a permission check before returning user data.
Medium: The form shows validation errors using color only. Add text and accessible state for screen readers.
Low: One helper function has unclear naming. Rename it to describe the returned value.

output_examples.output: The review reports a B score, one missing test update, no security blocker, and two cleanup suggestions.
The report flags non-virtualized rendering, repeated filtering during render, and a missing pagination strategy.

best_practices: Provide the branch diff, changed file list, and relevant project conventions before review.
Ask for a specific review focus when security, performance, or accessibility matters most.
Treat command examples as review aids and confirm write operations before applying fixes.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a generic review when only one risk area matters.
Do not accept severity labels without checking the cited file and line.
Do not run fix commands blindly in repositories with unrelated local changes.

faq.question: Does this skill edit code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides review guidance and may suggest commands. Any file changes should require explicit user approval.

faq.question: Can it review security issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes checks for injection, authentication, authorization, secrets, unsafe logging, and configuration mistakes.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What languages does it target?
faq.answer: The examples focus on TypeScript, React, and web applications, but the review checklists are broadly useful.

faq.question: Does it replace human code review?
faq.answer: No. It helps find issues and structure feedback, but humans must validate context and business impact.

faq.question: Why are some instructions in Japanese?
faq.answer: The source skill is written mainly in Japanese. Teams may translate prompts or outputs for broader use.
